pairs.why: Nearly identical; A's logs and stones are a bit more matte and painterly like the real cooking-pot card, while B's glowing log ends look slightly glossier.
A's logs, stones and kettle have more solid, wood- and stone-like form at the real cards' level of finish; B is a touch softer and more blurred.
A is the soft, flat, clay-like version (too smooth); B has more depth and crisper detail, like the real painterly cards.
B is softer and duller, while A has the moderately detailed, warmly lit painterly finish of the real cooking-pot card.
A is the over-smoothed clay-like version; B's stones, logs and fire have the crisper painterly modelling of the real cards.
B is the over-smoothed, flatter version; A's wood and stone have the moderate surface detail of the real cards.
A is again the soft, clay-like version; B is crisper and has livelier light, closer to the real cards.
